dialogue.content: (マッチングありがとうございます！本日はよろしくお願いします)
dialogue.English: (Thank you for matching with me! I look forward to our session today.)

dialogue.content: (こちらこそ、よろしくお願いいたします)
dialogue.English: (Likewise, I look forward to it as well.)

dialogue.content: （では始めさせていただきます。）
dialogue.English: (Alright, let's begin.)

dialogue.content: (よろしくお願いします)
dialogue.English: (Yes, please.)

dialogue.content: こんにちは、相談員です。今日はご相談ありがとうございます。最初に、年齢、性別、相談内容を教えて下さい。
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm the counselor. Thank you for reaching out today. To start, could you please tell me your age, gender, and the nature of your concern?

dialogue.content: 51歳、女性、小学生の息子の問題行動についての相談です。
dialogue.English: I'm 51, female, and I'd like to discuss the behavioral issues of my elementary school-aged son.

dialogue.content: 教えていただきありがとうございます。息子さんの問題行動ですね。詳しく聞かせていただけますか？
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that. Your son's behavioral issues, I see. Could you please tell me more about it?

dialogue.content: はい。3人きょうだいの末っ子なのですが、お姉ちゃんやお兄ちゃんのおやつなど、食べてはいけないものを勝手に冷蔵庫や戸棚から出して食べてしまいます。そして、食べたことがバレたら嘘をついてしまいます。
dialogue.English: Yes. He's the youngest of three siblings, and he takes and eats things he's not supposed to, like his older sister's or brother's snacks, from the fridge or cupboards without permission. And when he's caught, he lies about it.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。3人兄妹の年齢を教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: I see. Could you tell me the ages of the three siblings?

dialogue.content: 姉18歳、兄15歳、本人10歳です。本人が8歳頃の時からずっと続いてます。
dialogue.English: His sister is 18, his brother is 15, and he is 10. This has been going on since he was about 8 years old.

dialogue.content: では2年前くらいから始まった行動なんですね。そのことについて姉兄はなんと言っておられるんですか？
dialogue.English: So this behavior started about two years ago. What do his sister and brother say about it?

dialogue.content: お姉ちゃんは、呆れてますね。お兄ちゃんは、女子友から貰ったバレンタインのチョコレートも食べられてしまったので、激怒したりしてます。
dialogue.English: His sister is exasperated. His brother gets furious, especially since he once ate the Valentine's chocolate he received from a female friend.

dialogue.content: 兄ちゃんそれは激怒しますよね。お母さんもそのことが原因の兄弟喧嘩も心配になりますよね。
dialogue.English: I can imagine his brother would be furious about that. And I'm sure you also worry about the sibling fights it causes.

dialogue.content: 冷蔵庫に鍵を閉めたり、おやつを見つからないところに隠したり工夫をしてみましたが……探して食べてしまいます。なので、買い置きもやめたりしました。そうしたら、冷凍庫だけは鍵をかけられないので、冷凍庫のものを食べたりしましたね。お兄ちゃんは、賢い子なので、大人の対応ができる方で助かってはいます。
dialogue.English: I've tried things like putting a lock on the fridge and hiding snacks where he can't find them... but he searches for them and eats them. So, I stopped buying snacks to keep in the house. When I did that, he started eating things from the freezer, since that's the one place I can't lock. His older brother is a smart kid, so he's able to handle it maturely, which is a help.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。たくさん工夫されておられるんですね。お兄ちゃんしっかりしていますね。息子さんはなんでも食べてしまう感じなんですね。嘘はどういった嘘をつくんですか？
dialogue.English: I see. It sounds like you've tried many different things. His older brother seems very mature. So your younger son will eat just about anything. What kind of lies does he tell?

dialogue.content: 嘘の付き方なのですが……食べ物がなくなり皆が探し始めたら、「食べてない、俺じゃない」と始まりますね。その後、食べたゴミを至る所に隠しているやで、掃除した時にゴミが見つかるんです。そのゴミを息子に見せても嘘をつきますね。
dialogue.English: As for the lies... when food goes missing and everyone starts looking for it, he'll start by saying, "I didn't eat it, it wasn't me." Later, when I'm cleaning, I'll find the wrappers he's hidden in various places. Even when I show him the wrappers, he still lies.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。ゴミを見つけた際の嘘はなんて言うんですか？
dialogue.English: I see. What does he say when you show him the wrappers?

dialogue.content: 「食べてない、俺じゃない」って言います。その後、家族みんなが「他の家族は食べてないし、ゴミはゴミ箱に入れるから、○○しか食べたと考えられないよね」って責められ……渋々、食べたことを受け入れるパターンです。
dialogue.English: He says, "I didn't eat it, it wasn't me." Then, the whole family confronts him, saying, "None of the rest of us ate it, and we put our trash in the bin, so it must have been you." ...And then he reluctantly admits to eating it. That's the usual pattern.

dialogue.content: それを何百回も繰り返しているのです。
dialogue.English: We’ve been through that cycle hundreds of times.

dialogue.content: 最後は渋々受け入れるんですね。何百回もですか？！それは心配ですね。1週間のうちどのくらいの頻度でやっているんですか？
dialogue.English: So he does admit it in the end, albeit reluctantly. Hundreds of times?! That is concerning. How often does this happen in a week?

dialogue.content: ほぼ毎日に近いと思います。家族の目を盗んでするので、タイミング的には１階に1人になった時とか、家族が買い物とかで出かけて留守になった時とかですね。
dialogue.English: I think it's almost every day. He does it when no one is looking, so the timing is usually when he's alone on the first floor, or when the family is out shopping and he's home alone.

dialogue.content: なるほどですね。。渋々受け入れたあと息子さんはなんて言うんですか？
dialogue.English: I see... After he reluctantly admits it, what does he say?

dialogue.content: 最初は幼かったので、ダメなことをわかっていないのかと思い、しつけとして扱ってましたが……何度言っても繰り返す感じでした。怒られても怒られてもやります。
dialogue.English: At first, he was younger, so I thought maybe he didn't understand it was wrong, and I treated it as a matter of discipline... but he just kept repeating it no matter how many times I told him. He does it even if he gets scolded over and over.

dialogue.content: 受け入れたあとは、「わかった、もうやらない」と言ってましたね。でも、繰り返すんですよね。
dialogue.English: After admitting it, he would say, “Okay, I won’t do it again.” But then he repeats it.

dialogue.content: 色々な原因を私なりに探してみました。食べることが好きなのは間違いないのですが、病的に感じたので、過食症になっていたらどうしよう？と……本人に聞いてみましたが、上手く言葉で伝えられる年齢ではなく、色々と模索しましたが、やはりストレスが原因なのかな？と……
dialogue.English: I've tried to figure out the various causes myself. There's no doubt he loves to eat, but it felt pathological, so I worried, "What if he has a binge-eating disorder?" I tried asking him, but he's not at an age where he can express himself well with words. After exploring many possibilities, I've come to think that maybe stress is the cause...

dialogue.content: ストレスも色々なストレスがあると思うので、そのストレスの原因が今度はわからなく悩みました。本人がなんけ言葉で上手く表現できなく大変です。
dialogue.English: But there are many kinds of stress, so then I struggled because I didn't know the source of the stress. It's difficult because he can't express himself well with words.

dialogue.content: なんけ→なんせです。
dialogue.English: *Correction: なんせ.

dialogue.content: そうなんでね。もうわかったと言っても繰り返すんですね。病的に感じてしまうほどは不安になりますね。ストレスが原因と感じておられるんですね。
dialogue.English: I understand. So he says he understands, but then he repeats the behavior. It must be very worrying for you, to the point where it feels pathological. And you feel that stress is the cause.

dialogue.content: ストレスが原因なのは間違いないですね。あと、暇になると行動に移しますね。
dialogue.English: I'm sure stress is the cause. Also, he tends to do it when he's bored.

dialogue.content: 暇になると行動するんですね。息子さんとはよく普段会話はされますか？
dialogue.English: So he’s more likely to act when he’s bored. Do you and your son talk much in everyday life?

dialogue.content: 私には何でも話してくれますね。自発的に話すことはできても、表現力が乏しい感じなんです。自分でも自分の中で起きていることがきっとよくわかっていないんだと思います。漠然的にはわかってると思います。例えば、イライラしたから食べてしまったとか。そういうことは言ってました。なので、ストレスなんだと思いました。
dialogue.English: He tells me everything. He can initiate conversations, but he seems to lack expressive skills. I think he probably doesn't fully understand what's happening inside himself. He might have a vague idea. For example, he has said things like he ate because he was frustrated. That's why I thought it was stress.

dialogue.content: では、どんなことでイライラしたの？と聞くと……友達が嫌なことを言ってきたから、とかは言ってました。なので、友達関係もストレスなのはわかりました。先生のことも言ってましたね。
dialogue.English: When I ask, “What made you feel irritated?” he says things like, “A friend said something mean.” So I realized friendships are also a source of stress. He’s mentioned his teacher as well.

dialogue.content: 全て、対人関係ですね。あと、お父さんに怒られた時もイライラして勝手に食べてますね。
dialogue.English: It’s all interpersonal. Also, when his father scolds him, he gets irritated and eats without permission.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。息子さんとよく話をする関係は素敵ですね。息子さんの口からイライラしたから食べてしまったと言っていたんですね。そのストレスも対人関係なんですね。息子さんの事を真剣に思われてそこまでわかっていらっしゃるんですね。
dialogue.English: I see. It's wonderful that you have a relationship where you and your son can talk so much. So he himself said that he ate because he was frustrated. And that stress comes from his relationships with others. It shows how seriously you think about your son that you've been able to understand that much.

dialogue.content: ストレスが原因なのはわかったのですが、そのストレスを取り除きたいと思い息子と二人で色々と考えたのですが……相手があることなので本当に難しいですね。かと言って、息子が変わるとしても、やはりまだ小学生なので大変です。
dialogue.English: I understood that stress was the cause, so my son and I thought about various ways to remove that stress, but... it's very difficult because other people are involved. And even if my son were to change, it's hard because he's still in elementary school.

dialogue.content: 友達がバカにしてくるとか、先生が威圧的だとか……色々とストレスを抱えて食べることに走っているのはわかるのですが……解決策は本当に難しいです。
dialogue.English: Friends making fun of him, his teacher being intimidating... I understand that he's dealing with various stresses and turning to food... but finding a solution is really difficult.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。。ただ、お母さんと息子さんがよく普段からお話をしているとのことなので息子さんからしたらすごくストレスの軽減になっていると感じます。その対人関係について息子さんはどうしたいとかはなにか言っていましたか？
dialogue.English: I can imagine... However, you mentioned that you and your son talk often, and I feel that must be a great stress reliever for him. Has he said anything about what he'd like to do about those relationships?

dialogue.content: 友人関係に関しては、嫌な思いをしない友達が欲しいと言ってますね。でも、友達との付き合い方がまだ上手くできない時期なのもあり、困ってますね。他に良い友達を探すのも上手くいかず、嫌なことを言う友達と遊ばなければ良いのですが、お人好しなのと、遊びをしたいので誘われたら断れにいみたいです。
dialogue.English: Regarding his friendships, he says he wants friends who don't make him feel bad. But he's at an age where he's still not very good at navigating friendships, so it's a struggle. He hasn't had much luck finding other, better friends, and while it would be best not to play with the friends who say mean things, he's too good-natured and wants to play, so he can't seem to say no when they invite him.

dialogue.content: そこまで言葉にされてるんですね。嫌な思いをする友達との関係がよくなるといい方向に進みそうですね。
dialogue.English: He's able to put that much into words. It seems like things might move in a better direction if his relationship with the friends who make him feel bad improves.

dialogue.content: お母さんはその友達とお話をしたことはありますか？
dialogue.English: Have you ever spoken with those friends?

dialogue.content: 人のものは食べてはいけない事はわかっていると確信できましたので、あとはストレスを上手く発散できるようになることと、肥満になってきているので健康面も心配なことは、息子には繰り返し丁寧に伝えてます。
dialogue.English: I'm convinced he knows he shouldn't eat other people's things, so I've been repeatedly and carefully explaining to him that he needs to learn to relieve stress in a healthy way, and that I'm also worried about his health as he's starting to become overweight.

dialogue.content: そうなんですよ。その友達と話をしたくて、あえてしました。
dialogue.English: Yes, I have. I wanted to talk to that friend, so I made a point of doing so.

dialogue.content: 8歳～9歳までの時の一番のストレスの原因の子は、幼い頃から知っている子でした。その子は成長し、10歳になってからは息子に酷いことをしたりしなくなりました。「嫌だ、やめて」など、態度で示さないと相手に伝わらないことを私が息子に言ってから息子も頑張って言えるようになったからだとは思います。
dialogue.English: The child who was the biggest source of stress when he was 8 to 9 years old was someone we've known since he was little. That child has matured, and since turning 10, they've stopped being mean to my son. I think it's because I told my son that if he doesn't show his feelings with his attitude, saying things like "I don't like that" or "Stop it," the other person won't understand, and he's been trying hard to say those things.

dialogue.content: 10歳になってからは、転校してきた子がすごくストレスみたいです。転校生は一人寂しくて可哀想と思い誘って遊んでいたら、息子のことをバカにしてきて大変なストレスになっているそうです。息子は、優しいのですがお人好しなのでしょうね。
dialogue.English: Since he turned 10, a new student who transferred to his school seems to be a big source of stress. My son felt sorry for the new student being lonely and invited him to play, but now that student makes fun of him, which is causing a lot of stress. My son is kind, but I guess he's too much of a people-pleaser.

dialogue.content: 恩を仇で返されてる感じとも言えるみたいですね。
dialogue.English: It feels like his kindness is being repaid with ingratitude.

dialogue.content: そういう残念で悲しい気持ちがストレスとなって食べてしまうのですね。不器用でできないことが多い息子なので、色々と友達から言われることは多いのだと母親としてわかってはいます。でも、悪いこと何一つしていないので、可哀想で心配になりますね。
dialogue.English: So those disappointing and sad feelings become stress and lead to eating. As his mother, I know that since he's a bit clumsy and has trouble with many things, his friends probably say a lot to him. But he hasn't done anything wrong, so I feel sorry for him and worry.

dialogue.content: 健康面にまで影響を与えると心配ですね。態度で示せて、友達の対応が変わったんですね。主な原因は転校生だったんですね。
dialogue.English: It's certainly concerning when it starts to affect his health. It's great that he was able to show his feelings and his friend's behavior changed. So the main cause now is the new student.

dialogue.content: そうですね。今は間違いなく、転校生ですね。なので、その転校生と話をしてみたくて話をしてみました。息子とは違って、嘘のつく所がとても怖い感じがしました。息子に暴言吐いたことを担任とお母さんに嘘をついてました。息子は、そういう嘘はつけませんのでね。
dialogue.English: Yes. Right now, it's definitely the new student. So, I wanted to talk to that student, and I did. Unlike my son, I got a very scary feeling from the way he lies. He lied to his homeroom teacher and his mother about the verbally abusive things he said to my son. My son can't tell lies like that.

dialogue.content: 人を傷つける嘘は息子は絶対につきません。ただ、食べたものに関しては嘘をつきますが……
dialogue.English: My son absolutely does not tell lies that hurt people. Although, he does lie about the food he's eaten...

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。息子さんはそういう人を傷つけるような嘘はつかないんですね。色々お話を聞かせていただいて、息子さんのことをすごく思われているお母さんと、友達想いな息子さんだなと感じました。そろそろお時間になりますが、今日お話ししていかがでしたか？
dialogue.English: I see. So your son doesn't tell the kind of lies that hurt others. Hearing your story, I get the sense that you're a mother who thinks very deeply about her son, and that he is a very thoughtful friend. Our time is almost up. How do you feel after talking today?

dialogue.content: 理解していただき、ありがとうございます。私も息子のことや私の息子への思いなどが整理されとても有意義な時間となりました。今後に関しては、息子の「ストレスの発散の仕方と自分に合った友達との付き合い方を一緒に探して行こうね」って話をしていきたいと思いました。きっと、長い目で見守っていくことが一番大切なんだろうなぁと……子供の成長がきっと今回の問題も解決してくれるんだろうと見えてきました。ただ、肥満だけは心配ではありますね。
dialogue.English: Thank you for understanding. This has been a very meaningful time for me, as it's helped me organize my thoughts about my son and my feelings towards him. Moving forward, I want to talk with him and say, "Let's find ways to relieve stress and figure out how to interact with friends in a way that works for you." I've come to see that the most important thing is probably to watch over him with a long-term perspective... and that his own growth will likely solve this problem. However, I am still worried about his weight.

dialogue.content: 改めて、コミュニケーションと自己受容がポイントだと感じています。肥満に関しては、また分けて考えていくべきなのか？悩んでいます。
dialogue.English: I feel now that communication and self-acceptance are key. Regarding his weight, I'm wondering if I should think about that as a separate issue.

dialogue.content: その経験と成長が息子さんの未来にとても力になると思います。今は大変な時期かと思いますが、息子さんの成長を願っております。是非一緒に散歩などして健康面をサポートしつつその時お話をされてみてもいいかもしれませんね。
dialogue.English: I believe that this experience and his growth will be a great source of strength for your son's future. I know it must be a difficult time right now, but I am wishing for his growth. Perhaps you could support his health by going for walks together, and use that time to talk.

dialogue.content: そうですね。一緒に体を動かす機会を増やして、話もしてみたいと思います。
dialogue.English: That's a good idea. I'll try to create more opportunities for us to be active together and talk.

dialogue.content: 是非やってみてくださいね。少し時間が過ぎてしまいましたが、今日はご相談いただきありがとうございました。またいつでもお待ちしておりますので、遠慮なくお越しください。
dialogue.English: Please do. We've gone a little over our time, but thank you for your consultation today. Please feel free to reach out again anytime. We're always here for you.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。息子の未来への力となることに希望を持てました。たくさん励ましのお言葉をいただきありがとうございます。また機会がございましたら、よろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I feel more hopeful that this will become a source of strength for my son's future. Thank you for all your words of encouragement. I look forward to speaking with you again if the opportunity arises.

dialogue.content: こちらこそお時間をいただきありがとうございました。それでは失礼致します。
dialogue.English: Thank you for your time as well. I'll take my leave now.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: （15分もお時間過ぎてしまい失礼致しました。）
dialogue.English: (My apologies for going over time by 15 minutes.)

dialogue.content: (いいえ、私も話し過ぎてしまい、すみませんでした。)
dialogue.English: (Not at all. I’m sorry as well for talking too much.)

dialogue.content: （本日もクライアント役ありがとうございました。前回に続き2回目ですね。また機会がありましたらよろしくお願いします）
dialogue.English: (Thank you for playing the client role again today. This is the second time, following the last one. I look forward to working with you again if there's another opportunity.)

dialogue.content: (そうだったのですね。こちらこそ、ありがとうございます。大変勉強になりました。)
dialogue.English: (Oh, was it? Thank you as well. It was a great learning experience.)

dialogue.content: （こちらこそイメージもできて勉強になりました。それでは失礼致します。）
dialogue.English: (For me too, it helped me visualize the situation and was a good learning experience. I'll take my leave now.)
